subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw add a core public bootstrap-selection API and any command-backed bootstrap expansion, or should the remaining dynamic behavior stay in hooks/plugins?
rationale: The request crosses public config shape, prompt-cache stability, session-state routing, and command execution before prompt construction; source inspection can show the gap but cannot choose that product/security boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow core design
options.body: Add a small cache-stable session-type selector for bootstrap files and keep live time in dynamic runtime/tool surfaces while deferring command expansion until a sandbox/approval model is accepted.

options.title: Route dynamic behavior to hooks/plugins
options.body: Keep core hardcoded and require custom dynamic injection through agent:bootstrap hooks or a plugin, adding only missing hook API if maintainers identify one.

options.title: Let narrower PRs land first
options.body: Use the open tiered/session-scoped bootstrap PRs for partial relief, then revisit this umbrella only for the remaining command/time semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Add a small cache-stable session-type selector for bootstrap files and keep live time in dynamic runtime/tool surfaces while deferring command expansion until a sandbox/approval model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across the bootstrap filtering and system-prompt behavior that the decision would change.
